hosting.domain: Use the free HTTPS Render address or configure a custom domain. Set BETTER_AUTH_URL to exactly the chosen origin.
hosting.persistence: Production requires managed PostgreSQL and private cloud object storage. The local SQLite/files adapter is for development and tests only.

database.provider: Any compatible managed PostgreSQL service, including Supabase
database.connection: Use the provider's direct or session-pool connection URL. Keep DATABASE_URL in hosting secrets. TLS certificate verification is enabled; supply DATABASE_SSL_CA only if the provider needs an additional CA certificate.
database.migrations: Application tables and Better Auth tables are initialized on readiness. PostgreSQL advisory locks serialize schema initialization and shared mutations.
database.access: The application uses its own server-only schema. Do not expose twospace through Supabase's public Data API.

files.supabase: Create a private bucket named twospace-media. Set SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_STORAGE_BUCKET and a server-only SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY. A legacy SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is also supported. Never put these keys in NEXT_PUBLIC variables.
files.s3Alternative: Set the S3 variables and leave SUPABASE_URL unset. Configure the bucket as private and block public access using the provider's controls.
files.delivery: Images and recordings are read through membership-checked application endpoints. Raw storage URLs and credentials are not sent to the browser.

google.verification: Finish the provider consent-screen configuration and test a real account after deployment.

email.provider: Brevo or Resend, selected with EMAIL_PROVIDER. Existing configurations default to Resend.
email.brevo: For the free-address proof of concept, verify the sender address and complete Brevo's account requirements. Create an API key, then set EMAIL_PROVIDER=brevo, BREVO_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM in hosting secrets. EMAIL_FROM accepts an address or TwoSpace <address>. This integration uses the HTTPS API, not SMTP ports.
email.brevoLimit: Brevo temporarily replaces personal or unauthenticated sender addresses with a compliant address. Recipients may see that rewritten address. This is a temporary deliverability measure; Brevo recommends an authenticated custom domain for ongoing use. Account approval, plan limits, and recipient delivery still need a live check.
email.resend: Verify a sender domain, create a restricted sending API key, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend, RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM in hosting secrets.
email.configuration: Only the selected provider's key enables email features. Missing keys, unsupported providers, and invalid sender addresses are rejected. Configuration readiness does not prove that the provider has approved the sender or delivered an email.
email.externalDeliveryStatus: Verified on the hosted app on 2026-11-15: the password-reset request succeeded and Brevo reported delivery. Inbox placement and reset-token redemption were not checked; no user password was changed.
email.behavior: Cloud email accounts require email verification. Password resets use single-use Better Auth tokens and revoke existing sessions after a successful reset. Email features are unavailable until a delivery provider is configured.
checks: Verification creates a valid signed-in session
Reset email reaches an existing account
Used and expired reset tokens are rejected
Existing sessions stop working after reset
Unknown emails receive the same public reset response

verificationStatus: The hosted app passed Google sign-in, two synthetic cloud identities sharing updates, and private file access checks on 2026-11-15. Brevo confirmed reset-email delivery. Real partner onboarding and a full email-password reset remain user-driven checks.
accounts: Every shared space requires real signed-in accounts. Sample creation and profile switching are retired; historical sample records remain stored but cannot be accessed through legacy sample sessions.

nativeAuth.integration: Better Auth Expo server plugin 1.7.25, matching the web auth version.
nativeAuth.origins: Production trusts only BETTER_AUTH_URL and the twospace scheme. Browser origin and CSRF validation remain enabled. Expo Go exp:// URLs are not accepted in production; use an installed development or release build.
nativeAuth.requests: The native client stores its session using Expo SecureStore. REST requests send authClient.getCookie() in the Cookie header with credentials omitted. No API key or provider secret belongs in the app.
nativeAuth.google: The existing web OAuth callback remains BETTER_AUTH_URL + /api/auth/callback/google. The Expo plugin returns the completed session to the registered app scheme.
nativeAuth.verification: Local server integration covers native sign-in, stored-cookie REST access, callback restrictions, cross-site rejection and proxy redirect restrictions. Real iOS OAuth return still needs a device/build check.
